section: Infrastructure initiatives - power sector position, transport (ports, airports, highways, railways)
subsections: AP energy policies - objectives and targets

accepted.s:
The AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024, announced in June 2024, has set which of the following targets?
1. 160 GW of clean energy capacity
2. Net Zero by 2047
3. Investment of ₹10 lakh crore
4. Creation of 7.5 lakh jobs
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: The policy targets 160 GW of clean energy, Net Zero by 2047, ₹10 lakh crore investment and 7.5 lakh jobs.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when every statement reproduces a stated policy target.
accepted.sec: AP energy policies - objectives and targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration of Andhra Pradesh was made at Amaravati on:
accepted.x: The Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration was made at Amaravati on 19 July 2025.
accepted.tq: Fix the exact date and place of a policy declaration.
accepted.sec: AP energy policies - objectives and targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal objective of the Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration of Andhra Pradesh is to make the State the:
accepted.x: The declaration aims to make Andhra Pradesh the “Green Hydrogen Capital”.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related energy-sector titles.
accepted.sec: AP energy policies - objectives and targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Green Hydrogen Valley initiative in Andhra Pradesh seeks to reduce the cost of green hydrogen from approximately:
accepted.x: The declared objective is to reduce the cost from ₹460 per kg to ₹160–170 per kg.
accepted.tq: Compare the starting and target figures rather than merely recalling one number.
accepted.sec: AP energy policies - objectives and targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between the AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023 and the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024?
o: The 2023 policy was converted into a transport-only policy.
The 2024 policy replaced it with a coal-based energy framework.
The two policies operate as unrelated policies.
The 2023 policy was folded into the 2024 policy.
accepted.x: The AP Green Hydrogen and Green Ammonia Policy, 2023, was absorbed or folded into the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024.
accepted.tq: Test the relationship between two similarly named policies.
accepted.sec: AP energy policies - objectives and targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding progress under the AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024, is correct?
1. Approvals worth ₹2.88 lakh crore had been received.
2. These approvals were associated with 3.47 lakh jobs.
3. The Partnership Summit at Visakhapatnam on 14–15 November 2025 drew ₹4.54 lakh crore.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: approvals were worth ₹2.88 lakh crore and linked to 3.47 lakh jobs, while the Visakhapatnam Partnership Summit drew ₹4.54 lakh crore.
accepted.tq: Combine related progress figures and verify all numerical statements.
accepted.sec: AP energy policies - objectives and targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The nodal agency associated with the Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration in Andhra Pradesh is:
accepted.x: SRM University is identified as the nodal agency for the Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration.
accepted.tq: Apply the “which body performs this role?” identification method.
accepted.sec: AP energy policies - objectives and targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India’s first commercial green ammonia project is located at:
accepted.x: India’s first commercial green ammonia project is located at Kakinada.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the project location from other prominent energy and port locations.
accepted.sec: AP energy policies - objectives and targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following sets contains the National Green Hydrogen Mission hubs mentioned for Paradip, Kandla and Tuticorin?
accepted.x: The identified National Green Hydrogen Mission hubs are Paradip, Kandla and Tuticorin.
accepted.tq: Recognise the exact three-location set and avoid substituting major ports in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.sec: AP energy policies - objectives and targets  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In terms of the length of coastline among Indian States, Andhra Pradesh is stated to have the:
accepted.x: With the coastline figure of 1,053.07 km, Andhra Pradesh is ranked third among the States in the stated classification.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the current rank and the older rank associated with the 974 km figure.

accepted.s: Major ports and non-major ports are respectively covered under which Constitutional List entries?
o: State List Entry 27 and Union List Entry 31
Concurrent List Entry 27 and State List Entry 31
Union List Entry 31 and Concurrent List Entry 27
Union List Entry 27 and Concurrent List Entry 31
accepted.x: Major ports fall under Union List Entry 27, while non-major ports fall under Concurrent List Entry 31.
accepted.tq: Split the pair by both subject category and List entry.

accepted.s: The nodal body for non-major ports in Andhra Pradesh is the:
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board is the nodal body for non-major ports in the State.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority responsible for the specific port category.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Visakhapatnam — Major port under the Central Government
Krishnapatnam — Major port under the Central Government
Gangavaram — State-run port operated directly by APMB
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam is the major port of Andhra Pradesh and is under the Central Government. Krishnapatnam and Gangavaram are non-major ports, while Kakinada Anchorage is directly run by APMB.
accepted.tq: Find the correctly matched category and operator after eliminating swapped authorities.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Krishnapatnam — SPS Nellore district
b. Gangavaram — Visakhapatnam district
c. Mulapeta — Srikakulam district
d. Machilipatnam — Krishna district
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Krishnapatnam is in SPS Nellore, Gangavaram in Visakhapatnam, Mulapeta in Srikakulam and Machilipatnam in Krishna district.
accepted.tq: Start from sure district-port pairs and check the complete combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kakinada Deep Water Port — PPP OMST
accepted.x: Kakinada Anchorage is state-run and directly operated by APMB; it is not a PPP DBFOT port. Kakinada Deep Water, Gangavaram and Krishnapatnam are associated with OMST, BOOT and BOST models respectively.
accepted.tq: Find the single wrong operating-model match.

accepted.s: Which port is operated by Adani Krishnapatnam Port and is associated with the BOST model?
accepted.x: Krishnapatnam is a non-major port under the BOST model and is operated by Adani Krishnapatnam Port.
accepted.tq: Link the port, operating model and operator in one identification question.

accepted.s:
Which one of the following statements about Gangavaram Port is correct?
1. It is a non-major port in Visakhapatnam district.
2. It follows the BOOT model associated with 2003.
3. It is operated by Adani Gangavaram Port.
4. It has the deepest draft among the ports listed.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Gangavaram is a non-major Visakhapatnam-district port, follows the 2003 BOOT model, is operated by Adani Gangavaram Port and is noted for its deepest draft.
accepted.tq: Use the all-correct option after verifying category, year, operator and physical feature.

accepted.s: Which port has a 22 per cent revenue share accruing to the Government?
accepted.x: The Kakinada Deep Water Port, operated under the PPP OMST model, provides a 22 per cent revenue share to the Government.
accepted.tq: Associate the percentage with the correct port and operating model.

accepted.s: Which of the following ports is directly run by the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board?
accepted.x: Kakinada Anchorage is a state-run port directly operated by the Andhra Pradesh Maritime Board.
accepted.tq: Identify the direct state operator rather than a private concessionaire.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly represents the operators and stated capacities of the ports?
o: Kakinada Deep Water — Adani Gangavaram Port — 26 MTPA
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam is under the Central Government and has the stated capacity of 141.60 MTPA. The other options swap operators between ports.
accepted.tq: Use the operator-capacity pairing to detect swapped entities.

accepted.s: Which of the following is the correct descending order of the stated capacities of Krishnapatnam, Gangavaram and Kakinada Deep Water ports?
accepted.x: The stated capacities are 98 MTPA for Krishnapatnam, 64 MTPA for Gangavaram and 26 MTPA for Kakinada Deep Water.
accepted.tq: Arrange the figures by size before selecting the sequence.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with its stated cargo handled up to November 2025?
accepted.x: Krishnapatnam had the highest stated cargo of 41.09 MMT up to November 2025. The figures 24.39 MMT and 12.93 MMT relate to Gangavaram and Kakinada Deep Water respectively.
accepted.tq: Keep capacity figures separate from cargo-handled figures.

accepted.s: Non-major ports in Andhra Pradesh handled how much cargo up to November 2025?
accepted.x: The non-major ports handled 80.82 MMT up to November 2025.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an aggregate cargo figure from individual port capacities and progress percentages.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the greenfield ports of Andhra Pradesh is correct?
1. Ramayapatnam is in Nellore district and had 74.34 per cent progress.
2. Mulapeta is in Srikakulam district and had 61.91 per cent progress.
3. Machilipatnam is in Krishna district and had 48.35 per cent progress.
4. Kakinada Gateway is in Kakinada district and had 32.35 per cent progress.
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: All four statements correctly pair the greenfield ports with their districts and progress figures.
accepted.tq: Check each district-percentage pair before using the all-correct combination.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a greenfield port with its development model?
accepted.x: Ramayapatnam follows the SPV model. Mulapeta is associated with the landlord model, Machilipatnam with landlord/EPC, and Kakinada Gateway with PPP/DBFOT in the stated classifications.
accepted.tq: Separate the development models of similarly classified greenfield ports.

accepted.s:
Machilipatnam greenfield port is associated with which of the following features?
1. Landlord/EPC model
2. 35 MTPA capacity
3. Operational-limit reduction from 64 km to 15 km under the Indian Ports Act, 2025
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Machilipatnam is associated with the landlord/EPC model, a 35 MTPA capacity and the stated reduction of its operational limit from 64 km to 15 km.
accepted.tq: Combine project characteristics with a later statutory development.

accepted.s: The operational limit of Ramayapatnam was reduced from 51 km to 15 km under the Indian Ports Act, 2025. The corresponding reduction for Machilipatnam was from:
accepted.x: Machilipatnam’s operational limit was reduced from 64 km to 15 km, while Ramayapatnam’s was reduced from 51 km to 15 km.
accepted.tq: Compare two close statutory figures instead of confusing them with progress percentages.

accepted.s: Dugarajapatnam, identified for a greenfield port and shipbuilding cluster under the Shipbuilding Development Scheme, is in:
accepted.x: The greenfield port and shipbuilding cluster at Dugarajapatnam is in Tirupati district.
accepted.tq: Match the named project location with the correct district.

accepted.s: The four greenfield ports of Andhra Pradesh are stated to cost approximately ₹17,067 crore and add how much capacity?
accepted.x: The four greenfield ports are stated to cost ₹17,067 crore and add 108 MMTA capacity.
accepted.tq: Keep project cost, added capacity and long-term capacity targets distinct.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the port-capacity targets of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The capacity target is an additional 145 MTPA by 2030 and 300 MTPA by 2047.
accepted.tq: Read the time-bound target in chronological order and avoid reversing the milestones.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Mulapeta is in Srikakulam district and is associated with the landlord model in the greenfield-port classification; EPC is not its listed model in that table. Ramayapatnam is also identified with Prakasam in the port table, although older references used Nellore.
accepted.tq: Find the model mismatch while retaining the correct location and project identity.
